newsitem.title: THAILAND: Khmer Rouge's Ieng Sary, Cambodian ministers meet.
newsitem.headline: Khmer Rouge's Ieng Sary, Cambodian ministers meet.

text.p: Cambodia's co-defence ministers met dissident Khmer Rouge leader Ieng Sary in Bangkok on Thursday and discussed the prospects of a royal pardon for him and the integration of his breakaway group.

"We have met and held frank discussions in a good and sincere atmosphere. The meeting was successful, and we agreed to consider amnesty for him (Ieng Sary)," minister Tea Banh told reporters at his hotel here.
Ieng Sary heads the faction that last month split from the Maoist Khmer Rouge guerrilla group led by Pol Pot. Thursday's meeting was his first direct contact with top Cambodian leaders.

Ieng Sary was foreign minister during the Khmer Rouge reign of terror in the 1970s known as the "killing fields" during which more than one million people died of disease, starvation or overwork in labour camps.
The French-educated Ieng Sary, now in his 60s, was sentenced to death in absentia in 1979 for his role in the genocide. He was seen as Pol Pot's number two.

Now based in a jungle hideout in western Cambodia, he has been seeking a royal pardon since he broke with Pol Pot. Last month he formed the Democratic National United Movement to seek reconciliation with Phnom Penh.

"He (Ieng Sary) has made a major contribution for the unity and reconciliation of Cambodia by breaking away from the Khmer Rouge," Tea Banh said. "The government will certainly consider an amnesty for him."

Analysts said key obstacles to reconciliation with the dissident Khmer Rouge were the integration of the territory controlled by the breakaway faction into government hands and the question of what to do with Ieng Sary.
Tea Banh said he had agreed that government troops would enter areas controlled by Ieng Sary's forces in western Cambodia only if and when the dissidents asked for assistance.
Ieng Sary controls at least four major Khmer Rouge divisions with about 4,000 guerrillas, according to dissident sources.
The minister also said that Ieng Sary had confirmed at the meeting, held at a Thai guest-house, that he would recognise and abide by Cambodia's constitution.
Analysts believe Thursday's meeting could lead to direct talks between Ieng Sary and co-Premiers Hun Sen and Prince Norodom Ranariddh.
Meanwhile, Khmer Rouge rebels captured a northern Cambodian village held by the dissidents on Wednesday, the first seized by Pol Pot loyalists since the group's split.
